commit_message: GATE-09: Linux transparent networking — TUN adapter abstraction, DNS leak prevention, kill-switch, process lifecycle
scope_completed: DNS leak prevention: wouldDnsLeak() — rejects system DNS servers, blocks IPv6 AAAA queries when blockIpv6=true
Split tunneling: wouldBypassShareNet() — bypass domains for local traffic
KillSwitch: blocks all traffic when TUN is down (onTunStart/onTunStop/onTunFailure → block/unblock, enable/disable)
ProcessLifecycle: state machine (STOPPED→STARTING→RUNNING→DEGRADED→STOPPING→STOPPED), crash → auto-restart (max 3), kill-switch integration, event log
LinuxTunConfig: platform-specific (interfaceName, address, netmask, MTU=1400, routes, DNS)
PLATFORM_PROTOCOL_SEMANTICS_FORBIDDEN architecture guard (spec/16 §1: platform adapters must NOT create protocol semantics)
21 unit tests covering all policy/lifecycle/kill-switch scenarios
protocol_adr_references: spec/16-platforms.md §1 (platform adapters must NOT create protocol semantics)
known_limitations: Browser integration test (ordinary Linux browser reaches real HTTPS through ShareNet) is DEFERRED — it requires the full real-process stack: 3-message handshake → committed route → circuit setup → gateway forwarding → TUN device → browser. The protocol-core components all exist (GATE-03 through GATE-08), but they have not been wired together into a single end-to-end real-process integration. The unit tests prove the TUN adapter abstraction and policy/lifecycle correctness.

The TunAdapter interface is defined but not implemented for Linux (no real /dev/net/tun calls). A platform/linux/ implementation will use the interface but that requires root/system capabilities not available in the sandbox.

DNS leak prevention is enforced at the policy level (wouldDnsLeak check), but actual DNS interception (redirecting system DNS to the ShareNet proxy) requires the TUN device to be active and routing DNS queries.
The kill-switch blocks traffic logically (isBlocked() returns true), but actual network-level blocking (iptables/nftables rules) is not yet implemented.
